thought.text: The static export serves the `.html` files directly (path rewrite is the web server's job). Let me confirm direct file access works:

reasoning_content: In the static export, pages are served as .html files (e.g., `/ea-repository.html`), and the directory `/ea-repository/` is not created in the export. This is normal for a Next.js static export — a real web server (GitLab Pages, nginx) would rewrite the paths. Let me check whether the .html files are served directly, and also check whether the 404 fallback works.

action.command: for p in /ea-repository.html /eam-unterstuetzung.html /prinzipien-richtlinien.html /referenzarchitekturen.html /technologie-radar.html; do code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/sp.html -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:8080$p"); t=$(grep -oP '(?<=<title>)[^<]+' /tmp/sp.html|head -1); echo "$code  $p  $t"; done; ls /workspace/out/_next/ | head; du -sh /workspace/out

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "for p in /ea-repository.html /eam-unterstuetzung.html /prinzipien-richtlinien.html /referenzarchitekturen.html /technologie-radar.html; do code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/sp.html -w \"%{http_code}\" \"http://localhost:8080$p\"); t=$(grep -oP '(?<=<title>)[^<]+' /tmp/sp.html|head -1); echo \"$code  $p  $t\"; done; ls /workspace/out/_next/ | head; du -sh /workspace/out", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Curl exported HTML files directly"}
